name: PixiTween Director S24: turnaround (the real front, a Muse-drawn back, the true depth)
description: The 3D product stops showing its front on its back and stops guessing its depth. The real cut-out is placed in a three-panel sheet and Muse's image model draws the right side and the back beside it; code splits and measures the views (front kept, back the same outline, colours close, depth from the side), Muse checks them against the photo with one redraw at most; the body's front half wears the real photo, its back half the drawn (or a supplied) back, at the measured depth. The engine gets a back material for the body. Off by default (TURNAROUND=1); any failure keeps today's body. Leaves out: boxes, an image-to-3D mesh, characters, an approval gate.

readFirst: docs/architecture/turnaround-3d.md (the rule: the front is always the real photo; the spike's measured results; the flow; who does what)
debug/turnaround-spike/spike.ts and its outputs, if the owner linked debug/ into this worktree (the measured prompt, canvas and renders)
docs/architecture/sheet-film-3d.md (the s23 sheet film this PRD feeds)
server/product3d/prepare.ts, unwrap.ts, contour.ts (how the single-photo body is made today)
extraGuardrails: Start only on a branch that already holds the s23 sheet film: confirm server/crew/sheet-film/index.ts exports makeSheetFilm. If it does not, set notes to 'blocked: s23 not merged' and stop.
Run this PRD in its own git worktree (ralph/README.md section 3). Never edit files in the owner's main checkout: its dev server restarts on any server/ edit and kills a film that is building.
Every Muse call in code goes through ctx.meta.spark (chat or reviewImages) and is added to ctx.ledger like planBoard does. Tests fake ctx.meta.spark; nothing calls the network.

Creative choices stay with Muse (the board, the look, what to revise). Code draws the sheets, measures, checks rules and passes problems back to Muse as words; it never rewrites the board itself except to drop an element Muse named.

Renders in tests are faked: inject the render function (the shape of renderKeyFrames: (composition, times) => Promise<Buffer[]>) and return small sharp-made PNGs. Never launch Chromium in a unit test.

For a browser check never run `npm run dev` and never touch ports 8787, 8797, 5173 or 5199 (the owner's servers). Start your own pair and stop it after: `PORT=8798 DATA_DIR=data-s23 npx tsx server/main.ts` and `DIRECTOR_WEB_PORT=5180 DIRECTOR_API_URL=http://localhost:8798 npx vite --config web/vite.config.ts --port 5180 --strictPort`, then open http://localhost:5180.

debug/ is gitignored: the Clippy example sheets named in readFirst are reachable only if the owner linked debug/storyboard into this worktree. If they are missing, read the design doc's description of them instead; they are for the idea only.

THE RULE: the front of the product in the film is always the real photo. A drawn front is used only to line the views up and to measure that Muse kept it; it is never stored as a texture.

Drawn views are never painted on by code (no repainting, no label fixes). Trimming, resizing to the front's box and one global colour match are allowed (calibration). A failed view is redrawn by the image model once, or the film uses the single-photo body.
TURNAROUND is off by default; never turn it on by default in this PRD (the owner decides after MG-1).

stories.title: Turnaround prompt and the reference canvas
stories.description: As a drawer of the turnaround (the Muse image model), I want the real front placed in the sheet and a prompt that keeps it so that the side and back I draw are built round the true product.
steps: Read docs/architecture/turnaround-3d.md (the rule and the spike), debug/turnaround-spike/spike.ts if present (referenceCanvas and prompt are the measured starting point), server/art/invent-photo.ts and server/art/lint.ts (brand-term lint).
Create server/product3d/turnaround.ts exporting TURNAROUND_SIZE = { width: 1536, height: 1024 } and PANELS = 3.

Export referenceCanvas(cut: Buffer): Promise<{ png: Buffer; panel: Buffer }>: a white 1536 x 1024 canvas with the trimmed transparent cut-out fitted inside 88 % of the LEFT third's width and 90 % of the height, centred across the third, standing on a floor line at 95 % of the height; `panel` is the left third as drawn.

Export turnaroundPrompt(o: { what: string }): string: a turnaround sheet of three panels in one row; the left panel is the real product from the front and is kept exactly as it is; panel 2 is its right side (turned 90 degrees), panel 3 its back (turned 180 degrees); same size, height and floor line; same shape, materials, colours, cap and metalwork; the back shows what the back of this product really carries, small print as plain marks, never a new brand name or new words; orthographic, eye level, even soft shadowless light matching the left panel, pure white background, clear white space between panels, no floor shadow, no captions, no extra objects.
Take brand and person terms out of `what` with the lint helpers invent-photo uses.
Create server/product3d/turnaround.test.ts with sharp-made cut-outs.
acceptance: referenceCanvas of a 200 x 400 transparent rectangle returns a 1536 x 1024 PNG whose pixels outside the left third are all white
the product in referenceCanvas's left panel is centred across the third within 4 px and its bottom edge is at 95 % of the height within 4 px
turnaroundPrompt({ what: 'a bottle' }) contains 'right side', 'back', 'kept exactly' and 'pure white background', and never the words 'left side'

stories.title: Split the sheet into front, side and back
stories.description: As a step of the product build, I want the sheet cut into three transparent views and a measure of how well the front was kept so that the views can be checked and used.
steps: Read server/art/cutout-sheet.ts (whiteKeySheet, columnPieces), server/media/image.ts and server/product3d/turnaround.ts.
Export type TurnaroundViews = { front: Buffer; side: Buffer; back: Buffer } (trimmed transparent PNGs) from server/product3d/turnaround.ts.
Export splitTurnaround(ctx: ToolCtx, o: { sheet: Buffer; reference: { panel: Buffer } }): Promise<{ ok: true; views: TurnaroundViews; frontKept: number } | { ok: false; reason: string }>.

Resize the sheet to 1536 x 1024 first (the model may return another size). Use whiteKeySheet(ctx, { source, max: 3 }); exactly 3 pieces are required, in left-to-right order front, side, back (else ok false, reason 'found N views, need 3').
frontKept is the mean absolute difference (0 to 1, three decimals) between reference.panel and the sheet's left third, both resized to 96 x 256.
Create server/product3d/turnaround.split.test.ts with sharp-made sheets: three coloured shapes on white, two shapes, a blank sheet, and a sheet of a different size.
acceptance: a 1536 x 1024 sheet with three separated shapes returns ok true with the views in left-to-right order
a sheet with two shapes returns ok false and a reason that contains 'found 2 views'
a sheet whose left third equals the reference panel returns frontKept 0, and a 1024 x 683 sheet is split like its 1536 x 1024 copy

stories.title: Code checks that the views agree, and the measured depth
stories.description: As a gate before any model look, I want measured checks on the three views so that a drawing of another shape or colour is redrawn without a vision call, and the side gives the true depth.
steps: Read server/product3d/colour.ts (rgbToLab), server/product3d/pixels.ts and the TurnaroundViews type in server/product3d/turnaround.ts.
Create server/product3d/agree.ts exporting viewsAgree(o: { views: TurnaroundViews; frontKept: number }): Promise<{ ok: boolean; problems: string[]; depthShare: number }>.
depthShare = (side width / side height) / (front width / front height), rounded to two decimals: the product's depth as a share of its width.

Rules, each a problem sentence naming the view when it fails: (1) frontKept <= 0.08 ('the front panel was redrawn'); (2) the back's outline, scaled to the front's height and flipped left to right, overlaps the front's outline with intersection over union >= 0.85 ('the back is another shape'); (3) the back's mean Lab colour of opaque pixels is within distance 25 of the front's; (4) depthShare is between 0.15 and 1.25; (5) no view is more than 60 % transparent inside its own box.
Create server/product3d/agree.test.ts with sharp-made views.
acceptance: viewsAgree of three same-colour views of matching outlines and frontKept 0.02 returns ok true, no problems and depthShare equal to the side's aspect over the front's within 0.01
viewsAgree whose back is a triangle where the front is a rectangle returns ok false with a problem that mentions 'back' and 'shape'
viewsAgree with frontKept 0.2 returns ok false with a problem that mentions 'front', and one whose side is 3 times wider than the front returns a problem that mentions 'side'

stories.title: Muse checks the sheet against the photo
stories.description: As a reviewer (Muse, with the photo beside the sheet), I want to say whether the drawn side and back are the same product as the photo so that a wrong cage, cap, colour or invented mark is redrawn once.
steps: Read server/crew/sheet-film/check.ts (checkSheets: call shape, parsing, ledger) and debug/turnaround-spike/spike.ts if present (the check prompt that named real problems).

Create server/product3d/turnaround-check.ts exporting turnaroundCheckPrompt(o: { what: string; locks?: string[] }): string, parseTurnaroundCheck(raw: unknown): { ok: boolean; problems: string[] } and checkTurnaround(ctx, o: { photo: Buffer; sheet: Buffer; what: string; locks?: string[] }).

The prompt: the first picture is the real photo, the second a sheet of front, right side and back drawn from it; is the product in the side and back the same physical product (shape, cap, metalwork, glass, label art, colours); is anything invented (a lump, a new mark, new words); does the side read as the depth of the real product; the lock lines when given; reply JSON {"ok":boolean,"problems":[string]} with at most 4 problems.
parseTurnaroundCheck reads JSON in a code fence or with text around it; anything unreadable gives ok true and no problems (the check never blocks a film).

parseTurnaroundCheck('no json here') returns ok true and an empty problems list

stories.title: The back texture: fitted to the front and colour-matched
stories.description: As a 3D body builder, I want the drawn back laid in the front texture's own box and colour so that the back half lines up with the real front at the sides.
steps: Read server/product3d/prepare.ts (how the front texture of shape 'other' is trimmed and sized), server/product3d/contour.ts and server/product3d/pixels.ts.
Create server/product3d/back.ts exporting backTexture(o: { back: Buffer; front: Buffer }): Promise<Buffer>, where front is the front texture PNG as prepareProduct3D stores it.
Trim the back view and resize it to exactly the front texture's width and height (fill: the outlines match by rule 2 of viewsAgree).

Colour match: on pixels opaque in both, shift each RGB channel of the back so its mean and standard deviation equal the front's (clamped 0 to 255); keep the back's own alpha. This is calibration; nothing else is painted.
Create server/product3d/back.test.ts with sharp-made pictures.
acceptance: backTexture returns a PNG of exactly the front texture's width and height
a back of mean grey 100 against a front of mean grey 160 comes back with a mean within 3 of 160 on opaque pixels

stories.title: Engine: the body's back half wears its own picture
stories.description: As a 3D engine, I want an extruded body to take a second picture for its back half so that a turned product shows its back instead of its front read the other way.
steps: Read engine/src/three/build/geometry.ts (buildBody: the front and back halves, their UVs), engine/src/three/build/object.ts (how the extrude material is made, the sideColor material array), engine/src/three/build/materials.ts and the engine's object spec type for `material.map`.
In buildBody add two geometry groups: group 0 the front half's indices, group 1 the back half's (including the side wall each half owns). Without a back picture everything renders as before.

Add an optional `backMap` (texture id) beside `map` in the engine's material spec; in object.ts, for an extrude with `section` and a backMap, use a material array [front material, the same material with map = backMap]; alphaTest stays 0.5 on both.
Keep the back half's UVs as they are (read the other way so a drawn back is not mirrored): a back picture drawn as seen from behind appears the right way round.
Add tests in engine/src/three/build/geometry.test.ts and a new engine/src/three/build/object.test.ts case.
acceptance: buildBody returns a geometry with exactly 2 groups whose counts add up to the index count
a body vertex on the back half at the largest x has a back u within 0.05 of 0 (the drawn back's left edge is the viewer's left when looking from behind)
buildObject for an extrude with section and backMap gives a mesh with 2 materials whose maps are map and backMap, and without backMap gives one material as before

stories.title: turnaroundFor: draw, split, agree, check, redraw once, or fall back
stories.description: As a pipeline step for the product, I want one function that turns a photo and its cut-out into checked views and a depth, or a plain reason, so that a film never fails because of the turnaround.
steps: Read server/product3d/turnaround.ts, agree.ts, turnaround-check.ts, back.ts and server/env.ts (how booleans that are off by default are declared).
Add TURNAROUND to server/env.ts as a boolean off by default, and to .env.example as TURNAROUND=0.

Create server/product3d/turnaround-flow.ts exporting turnaroundFor(ctx, o: { photo: Buffer; cut: Buffer; what: string; locks?: string[]; log: (line: string) => void }): Promise<{ views: TurnaroundViews; sheet: Buffer; depthShare: number } | undefined>.

Steps: drawTurnaround, splitTurnaround, viewsAgree; when they pass, checkTurnaround. Any problem from any step: redraw once with `extra` = the problems and run the steps again; a second failure returns undefined and logs 'turnaround: <reason>, using the single-photo body'.
Run checkTurnaround only on a sheet that passed viewsAgree (no vision call on a sheet code already refused).
Cache the result in the process by the sha1 of the photo bytes, so the same photo is drawn once; a failure is not cached.
Every thrown error becomes undefined plus the log line; nothing here throws. Returns undefined at once, with no call, when TURNAROUND is off.

when both sheets fail or drawTurnaround rejects, turnaroundFor resolves to undefined and logs a line that contains 'single-photo body'; a second call with the same photo after a success makes no new draw
